title: NCQ: Code reuse support for Node.js developers
utc_basis: byte recheck after direct reading; first reading occurred earlier in this session
version: author-hosted version as retrieved; SHA256 in source-retrievals.json
findings: Two sequential baseline-first within-person cohorts; different tasks per condition, five-task balanced assignment. First comparison suppresses search in the same REPL; second changes editor, search, ranking, correction and execution support. Task success is executable JavaScript satisfying the specification. Timestamped inputs and recordings were collected; installation marks package selection. Final analyzed cohorts each contain ten people. Snippet visibility, attempted reuse and successful reuse are distinguished.
limitations: No downloadable participant timing/assignment/scoring table is linked beyond the tool repository. Twenty minutes is a planning estimate, not a verified enforced cap. Training/video precede tasks; activity intervals and later rework are absent. A 1–7 confidence response is not objective quality. Figure distributions cannot supply exact raw timings; matching P labels between cohorts is invalid.
